mainTopic: Acquiring ownerless land, שמואל's rules on government law and taxes, and what divides one field from another
overview: The amud opens by finishing a court case about someone who hoed a field that a Jew had bought from a non-Jew. The judge follows רב, who says one hoe-stroke acquires the whole field, and רב הונא בר אבין sends a ruling that the second Jew keeps such a field. Next, רבה reports three rules of שמואל: דינא דמלכותא דינא, Persian sharecropping runs up to forty years, and land sold by tax officials for land tax (טסקא) may be bought. The גמרא limits the third rule to land tax and not head tax (כרגא), but רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע says everything a person owns is pledged even for head tax. אמימר challenges him from the בכור's double share, הונא בר נתן answers, and a report that the הלכה follows him is rejected. רב אשי then rules that an idler must help the town with its taxes when the town got him relief. Finally, two reports of רבי יוחנן disagree on whether a boundary strip or sea squill divides fields only for taking a convert's property or also for פאה and טומאה. The גמרא begins quoting a משנה that lists what divides a field for פאה, and the list continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The litigant asks to use שמואל's narrow rule
steps.stepSummary: The person who lost the field asks the judge at least to follow שמואל's other ruling, so the hoer gets only the spot he struck.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let the Master rule for me like שמואל's other statement, since שמואל said: he acquires only the spot his hoe struck!
steps.whatsHappening: The losing party in the court case pushes back on the judge. He says: if you follow שמואל on the main issue, follow שמואל here too and give the hoer only the spot he hoed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the judge followed שמואל's rule that a non-Jew's property is like ownerless desert land, so whoever takes possession first gets it. The litigant points out that שמואל also said hoeing acquires only the exact spot struck. He wants to cut his loss down to that small spot.

keyTerms.meaning: Let the Master do (rule) for me
The spot struck by his hoe

phrases.english: Let the Master do for me
according to the other statement of Shmuel,
as Shmuel said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא קָנָה אֶלָּא מְקוֹם מַכּוֹשׁוֹ בִּלְבַד!
phrases.english: He acquired only the spot of his hoe-stroke!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the court case from before this section, where the judge followed שמואל's rule about a non-Jew's property.
steps.kashyaTarget: The judge's ruling that the hoer acquires the whole field
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the judge follows שמואל on one point, he should be consistent and follow שמואל's narrow rule that hoeing acquires only the spot struck.

steps.title: The judge follows רב: one stroke acquires everything
steps.stepSummary: The judge answers that on this point he holds like רב, who says one hoe-stroke acquires the whole field.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: On this point I hold like our teaching, as רב הונא said in the name of רב: once he struck it with one hoe-stroke, he acquired all of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The judge turns down the request. On how much a hoe-stroke acquires, he follows רב and not שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The judge can follow שמואל on one question (a non-Jew's land is like ownerless land) and רב on another question (how much a hoe-stroke acquires). Each question is decided on its own, so he does not have to follow the same אמורא on both. The result is that the hoer keeps the entire field.

keyTerms.meaning: Like our teaching (the ruling of our school)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב, one hoe-stroke on a field acquires the whole field. Here the judge mixes שמואל's rule on one point with רב's rule on another.

phrases.english: He said to him: In this matter,
I hold in accordance with our teaching –
as Rav Huna said in the name of Rav:
once he struck it with one hoe-stroke –
he acquired all of it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: בְּהַאי, אֲנָא כִּשְׁמַעְתִּין סְבִירָא לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the litigant's request in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Choosing a different authority on a separate question
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Following שמואל on one point means following him on every related point.
steps.terutzMaskana: The judge follows רב on how much a hoe-stroke acquires, so the hoer gets the whole field.

steps.title: רב הונא בר אבין: the second Jew keeps the field
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר אבין sends a ruling that if a Jew buys a field from a non-Jew and another Jew takes possession of it, it is not taken away from the second Jew. Other sages agree.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר אבין sent: A Jew who bought a field from a non-Jew, and another Jew came and took possession of it — we do not take it away from him. And so רבי אבין, רבי אילעא, and all our Rabbis agreed on this.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ruling arrives that matches the case we just saw. A second Jew who takes possession of a field bought from a non-Jew keeps it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Paying money alone does not complete the purchase from the non-Jew, so until the buyer does an act of possession (חזקה), the land is treated as ownerless. Whoever takes possession first, like the second Jew, wins. The list of agreeing sages shows this was a widely accepted ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Sent (a ruling, usually from ארץ ישראל)
Took possession (did an act of ownership)

steps.whyThisMatters: It backs up the ruling in the court case: a field bought from a non-Jew stays open to anyone until the buyer takes possession.

phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Avin sent:
A Jew who bought a field from a gentile,
and another Jew came and took possession of it –
we do not take it out of his hand.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן הָיָה רַבִּי אָבִין וְרַבִּי אִילְעָא
phrases.english: And so too Rabbi Avin and Rabbi Ile'a
and all our Rabbis agreed on the matter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a sent ruling that supports the outcome of the court case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A second Jew who takes possession of a field a Jew bought from a non-Jew keeps it.

steps.title: שמואל's three rules about the government and land
steps.stepSummary: רבה reports three rules of שמואל: the law of the kingdom is binding, Persian sharecropping runs up to forty years, and a sale by tax officials of land seized for land tax is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: These three things were told to me by עוקבן בר נחמיה the ריש גלותא in the name of שמואל: The law of the kingdom is the law; Persian sharecropping is up to forty years; and these tax officials who sell land for land tax — their sale is a valid sale.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching with three related rules of שמואל about how government law affects owning land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first rule, דינא דמלכותא דינא, is the basis for the other two. Because government law is binding, Persian rules about land and the tax officials' seizure of land for unpaid land tax count in הלכה. So a Jew may buy land that the officials sold for land tax.

keyTerms.meaning: The law of the kingdom is the law (binding)
The Exilarch, head of the Jews in בבל
Their sale is a valid sale

steps.whyThisMatters: דינא דמלכותא דינא became one of the basic principles of הלכה about how Jews relate to government law.

phrases.english: Rabba said: These three things

phrases.aramaic: אִישְׁתַּעִי לִי עוּקְבָן בַּר נְחֶמְיָה רֵישׁ גָּלוּתָא,
phrases.english: were told to me by Ukvan bar Nechemya the Exilarch,
in the name of Shmuel:
The law of the kingdom is the law;
and Persian sharecropping – up to forty years;
phrases.notes: The גמרא doesn't spell this out. The idea is that under Persian law, claims to own land are judged by a forty-year span.

phrases.english: and these tax officials who sell land for the land tax –
their sale is a valid sale.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: three rules from שמואל about government law and land.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Government law is binding; Persian sharecropping lasts up to forty years; land sold by tax officials for land tax may be validly bought.

steps.title: Only for land tax, not head tax
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא limits the third rule: a sale is valid only if the land was seized for land tax, not for head tax.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this applies to land tax, but for head tax — no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows שמואל's third rule. It applies only to land tax (טסקא) and not to head tax (כרגא).
steps.deeperAnalysis: If tax officials take land to cover a person's head tax, the sale is not valid, and buying that land would mean buying stolen property. The reason comes in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: Head tax (a tax on each person)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two taxes: טסקא is a tax on land, and כרגא is a tax on each person.

phrases.english: And this applies to land tax,
but for head tax – no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the third rule from step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sales by tax officials are valid only for land seized for land tax, not for head tax.

steps.title: Why the difference?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why a sale for head tax is not valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the limit in step 5. This sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both are government taxes, so it is not obvious why one would allow the officials to sell land and the other would not. The גמרא wants the logic.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why land seized for head tax may not be validly sold

steps.title: Head tax sits on the person, not the land
steps.stepSummary: Head tax is a charge on the person himself, so his land is not pledged for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Head tax rests on the man's head.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that head tax is owed by the person and has nothing to do with his land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Land tax is tied to the land, so the government may seize and sell the land for it. Head tax is tied only to the person, so selling his land for it is theft, and the sale is not valid.

phrases.english: Head tax – it rests on the head of the man.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Head tax is a personal obligation, so the person's land is not pledged for it.

steps.title: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע: everything is pledged for head tax
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע disagrees: all of a person's property, even barley in a jug, is pledged for head tax.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא the son of רב יהושע said: even the barley in the jug is pledged for head tax.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא disagrees with the limit in step 5. He says all of a person's property is pledged even for head tax.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By his view, head tax is not only 'on the head.' All of a person's belongings, down to a little barley in a jug, can be taken for it. So a sale by tax officials for head tax would also be valid.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two views. One says only land tax allows officials to sell land. רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע says even head tax lets them take all of a person's property.

phrases.aramaic: רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אָמַר:
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua said:
Even the barley in the jug
is pledged for the head tax.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the limit in steps 5 and 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All of a person's property, even small movable items, is pledged for head tax.

steps.title: אמימר's challenge: the בכור would lose his double share
steps.stepSummary: אמימר challenges רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע: if all property is pledged for head tax, a father's estate becomes only 'potential' property, and a בכור does not take a double share of potential property.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: הונא בר נתן told me that אמימר raised a difficulty against this. If so, you have cancelled the inheritance of the firstborn son. The estate would count as 'potential' property, and the firstborn does not take a double share of potential property the way he does of property the father actually held.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a challenge, through רב אשי and הונא בר נתן, against the view in step 8 that everything a person owns is pledged for head tax.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the king can take anything the father owned to cover his head tax, then nothing he leaves is fully 'his'. It is only property the sons might end up getting. The rule is that a בכור gets a double share only of what the father actually held, not of what was only 'coming' to him. So the בכור's double share would almost never apply.

keyTerms.meaning: firstborn son, who normally inherits a double share
'potential' property, which is not yet in the father's hands
property the father actually held at his death

steps.confusionAlert: The challenge does not say the sons lose everything. It says the בכור loses his EXTRA double share, because that extra share applies only to property the father actually held.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: אֲמַר לִי הוּנָא בַּר נָתָן,
phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: Huna bar Natan said to me,
Ameimar raised a difficulty with it:
phrases.notes: 'It' is רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע's rule from step 8, that everything is pledged for head tax.

phrases.aramaic: אִם כֵּן, בִּטַּלְתָּ יְרוּשַּׁת בְּנוֹ הַבְּכוֹר –
phrases.english: If so, you have cancelled the inheritance of his firstborn son –
since it is 'potential' property,
and the firstborn does not take a double share in potential property as he does in held property.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָשֵׁי בַּהּ אַמֵּימָר: אִם כֵּן, בִּטַּלְתָּ יְרוּשַּׁת בְּנוֹ הַבְּכוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the rule stated in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע's rule that all property, even barley in a jug, is pledged for head tax.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If everything is pledged, the estate is only 'potential' property (רָאוּי), so the בכור's double share would almost never apply. That cannot be right.

steps.title: הונא בר נתן's reply: the father paid before he died
steps.stepSummary: הונא בר נתן answers אמימר: the same problem would exist with land tax, and there you must say the father paid and then died. So too with head tax.
steps.simpleTranslation: I said to him: If so, the same problem would exist even with land tax! Rather, what do you have to say there? That he paid the land tax and then died. Here too, he paid the head tax and then died.
steps.whatsHappening: הונא בר נתן defends the rule from step 8 by showing that אמימר's question would hit land tax too, which everyone agrees is a claim on land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Land tax certainly lets the king take land, yet the בכור still gets his double share. The reason must be that we are talking about a father who paid his tax before he died, so his land was free and clear. The same answer works for head tax: if the father paid it before dying, nothing hangs over the estate.

keyTerms.meaning: head tax, a charge on the person
'rather, what must you say?', which turns the questioner's own answer back on him

phrases.english: I said to him: If so,
phrases.notes: 'I' is הונא בר נתן, still speaking, and 'him' is אמימר.

phrases.english: even land tax too [would have this problem]!
Rather, what do you have to say [there]?
That he paid the land tax and then died;
here too – he paid the head tax and then died.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי לֵיהּ: אִי הָכִי, אֲפִילּוּ טַסְקָא נָמֵי
steps.terutzResolutionType: Parallel case: the same question applies to land tax, and the answer there also works here.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since all property is pledged for head tax, the estate is only 'potential' property.
steps.terutzMaskana: We are talking about a father who paid his tax before he died, so the estate is fully held, and the בכור takes his double share.

steps.title: Report that רבא's scribes ruled like רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע
steps.stepSummary: הונא בר נתן reports that he asked רבא's scribes, and they told him the הלכה follows רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: הונא בר נתן told me: I asked רבא's scribes, and they told me the הלכה follows רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע.
steps.whatsHappening: A ruling is reported in support of the view that all property is pledged for head tax. The גמרא will judge this report in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is new information: a practical ruling from the court of רבא, offered to settle the argument. If it holds, a person's movable goods could be taken for his head tax.

keyTerms.meaning: scribes who wrote the court's documents and rulings

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי, אָמַר לִי הוּנָא בַּר נָתָן:
phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: Huna bar Natan said to me:
I asked the scribes of Rava,
and they said to me:

phrases.aramaic: הִלְכְתָא כְּרַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ.
phrases.english: The halakha is like Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁאֵילְתִּינְהוּ לְסָפְרֵי דְרָבָא, וַאֲמַרוּ לִי: הִלְכְתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending the rule, הונא בר נתן brings a report that the הלכה follows it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבא's scribes, the הלכה follows רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע: all property is pledged for head tax.

steps.title: The גמרא rejects the report
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the report is not reliable: it was said only to back up his own position.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that is not so. There, he said it only to support his own statement.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes aside the ruling reported in step 11 and does not accept it as the final הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא does not attack the reasoning. It doubts the report itself, because it was said to strengthen the speaker's own view. So the ruling like רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע is not accepted on the strength of this report.

keyTerms.meaning: 'but it is not so', which rejects what was just said
to hold up / support his own statement

steps.whatToRemember: The claim that all property is pledged for head tax is not accepted as the final הלכה on the basis of this report.

phrases.english: But it is not so,
there – it was to support his own statement that he said it.
phrases.notes: 'His own statement' is the position he defended against אמימר in step 10.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא הִיא, הָתָם לְאוֹקוֹמֵי מִילְּתֵיהּ הוּא דְּאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the report given in step 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the report that the הלכה follows רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The report was said to support the speaker's own position, so it cannot be relied on as a ruling.

steps.title: An idler must help the town pay its taxes
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי rules that an idler (פַּרְדָּכְתְּ) must help the town with its tax burden.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב אשי said: An idler must help the town.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling of רב אשי about town taxes. It opens a new short topic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even a person who does no work and earns nothing there must share in the town's tax payments. The next step limits when this applies.

keyTerms.meaning: helps the town (pays his share of its taxes)

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: פַּרְדָּכְתְּ – מְסַיַּיע מָתָא.
phrases.english: And Rav Ashi said: An idler – must help the town.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: פַּרְדָּכְתְּ מְסַיַּיע מָתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ruling on a related tax topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An idler must contribute to the town's tax burden.

steps.title: Limit: only when the town saved him
steps.stepSummary: The rule applies only when the town got him off. If the tax collectors themselves skipped him, it is help from Heaven, and he does not have to pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this applies when the town saved him. But if it was the tax collectors who let him go, that is help from Heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא limits רב אשי's rule from step 13 and shows when the idler must help and when he need not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the town worked to get him a lighter load, he owes the town his share in return. But if the tax collectors on their own did not go after him, no one in the town did him a favor. His luck is a gift from Heaven, and he keeps it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'and these words apply...', which introduces a limit on a rule

steps.whatToRemember: The idler pays only when the town saved him from his tax. If the collectors simply passed him over, it is help from Heaven, and he owes nothing.

phrases.english: And this applies where the town saved him,
but [if it was] the tax collectors – it is help from Heaven.
phrases.notes: He means the collectors, on their own, did not come after him, so he got off without the town's help.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: The idler must help only if the town obtained his relief. If the tax collectors skipped him, he keeps the benefit as help from Heaven.

steps.title: A boundary or sea squill divides fields only for a convert's property
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי in the name of רבי יוחנן: a מצר or חצב divides fields for נכסי הגר, but not for פאה or טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: A boundary strip and a sea squill plant act as a divider when people take a convert's property. But for פאה and טומאה, they do not act as a divider.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a ruling from רבי יוחנן, reported by רב אסי, about when a field marker splits one field into two.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a גר dies with no heirs, his land is ownerless and anyone can take it. If someone takes one part, he gets only up to the מצר or חצב, not the land past it. But for the laws of פאה and טומאה, this same marker does not make two separate fields.

keyTerms.meaning: Sea squill, a plant set in the ground to mark a border
Act as a divider, splitting one field into two
The property of a convert who died with no heirs, which anyone may take
The corner of the field that is left for the poor

steps.confusionAlert: This does not say the marker is never a real boundary. It counts as a divider for one law (taking a convert's property), and this report says it does not count for two other laws.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rav Asi said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
The boundary strip and the sea squill divide fields regarding the property of a convert,
phrases.notes: Someone who takes a dead convert's field gets it only up to this marker, not past it.

phrases.english: but regarding פאה and ritual impurity, they do not.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the tax rulings of steps 4-14 and goes back to acquiring ownerless property (נכסי הגר), the same subject as the hoeing case in steps 1-3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מצר or חצב splits fields for taking נכסי הגר, but not for פאה or טומאה.

steps.title: A second report says they divide even for פאה and טומאה
steps.stepSummary: רבין reports that רבי יוחנן said the מצר and חצב divide fields even for פאה and טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבין came from ארץ ישראל, he said in the name of רבי יוחנן: They act as a divider even for פאה and טומאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different report of what רבי יוחנן said, and it disagrees with רב אסי's report.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אסי's report limited the divider to a convert's property. רבין's report widens it: the מצר and חצב split a field for פאה and טומאה as well. Now we have two versions of one teacher's view.

keyTerms.meaning: When רבין came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל), bringing a teaching

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אֲתָא רָבִין אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: When Ravin came, he said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
Even for פאה and ritual impurity.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רָבִין אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of רבי יוחנן's ruling that disagrees with step 15 on פאה and טומאה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מצר or חצב splits fields even for פאה and טומאה.

steps.title: What is the case of פאה here?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how dividing a field matters for the laws of פאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case of פאה, what is it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask a clarifying question: how does it matter for פאה whether this is one field or two? This sets up the source it is about to quote.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both reports mention פאה, but it is not yet clear how a field divider affects it. The גמרא wants the background case before going on.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it? (a request to explain a case)

phrases.english: פאה, what is it?
phrases.notes: He is asking how splitting a field makes a difference for the law of פאה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for background on the פאה case mentioned in steps 15 and 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How a field divider matters for the law of פאה.

steps.title: A משנה lists things that divide a field for פאה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה: a stream and a canal divide a field for פאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: These things divide a field for פאה: a stream, and a canal...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question by starting to quote a משנה that lists things that cut a field into separate fields for פאה. The list continues past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If something divides the field, each part counts as its own field and needs its own פאה. That is how the question of one field or two matters for פאה. The first items listed are a stream and a canal.

phrases.english: As we learned: And these divide a field for פאה:
phrases.notes: This משנה is in מסכת פאה, פרק ב. Each part of a divided field gives its own פאה.

phrases.english: a stream, and a canal,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 17 by quoting the משנה about dividers for פאה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A divider makes each part a separate field for פאה, as the משנה lists: a stream, a canal, and more.
